title: 說文解字 (Shuowen Jiezi), Ming Jiguge 汲古閣 edition, full scan

license_or_reuse: Public domain (PD-scan of PD original)

annotation: Page layout shows seal-form head character above regular-script entry, with 重文 (variant) forms listed beneath — the variant-character concept made physical
designer_lesson: How a dictionary physically encodes standard form vs variant; where to look when verifying a seal-script claim
limits: Han-era etymologies partly superseded by oracle-bone palaeography; large PDF, browse by juan

title: 康熙字典 (Kangxi Dictionary), Daoguang 7 (1827) reprint, sample page

license_or_reuse: Public domain (1827 print; PD-old)
relevance: The Qing-era standard reference grid: 214 radicals, 47,035 characters, 反切 glosses
annotation: Large head character, double-column small glosses, citations of earlier word-books; the look of pre-modern lexicographic authority
designer_lesson: The baseline page layout against which any 'classical dictionary' styling in the family book can be judged
limits: File page not fully re-verified this session (thumbnail confirmed embedded on zh.wikipedia 康熙字典 article); known citation errors in the work itself (see 王引之 字典考證)

title: 8 strokes of 永-zh.svg (Eight Principles of Yong diagram)
creator: Yug / Rhynyx (derivative)
license_or_reuse: CC BY-SA 2.0 (attribution + share-alike required)
relevance: Visual bridge between character anatomy (strokes) and calligraphic gesture (八法)
annotation: Numbered diagram makes explicit that 永 has 5 written strokes but embodies 8 brush principles; direction arrows show gesture order
designer_lesson: Stroke count ≠ gesture count; essential when reasoning about what cursive abbreviation removes vs preserves
limits: Modern didactic diagram, not a historical artefact; CC BY-SA requires attribution if reproduced in the book

title: 宋拓 智永《真草千字文》冊 (關中本, Song rubbing)
creator: Zhiyong 智永 (Sui); engraved 1109 by Xue Sichang 薛嗣昌
institution: Palace Museum, Beijing (original stones: Xi'an Beilin)
license_or_reuse: Institutional page; image reuse per Palace Museum terms (not open-licensed — verify before reproduction)
relevance: Systematic side-by-side of regular (真) and cursive (草) forms of identical characters
annotation: Each line pairs the 楷書 and 草書 of the same text — lawful, attested cursive abbreviation made visually checkable
designer_lesson: The single best training set for judging whether a cursive form is attested or invented
limits: No confirmed open-licence direct image found this session; use page for study, seek licensed reproduction (or NPM/NDL alternatives) for print

title: 神龍本 蘭亭序 (Lanting Xu, Shenlong version)
creator: Trad. Feng Chengsu 馮承素 (Tang), after Wang Xizhi 王羲之 (353)
object_id: (故宮藏 馮摹蘭亭序卷; 24.5×69.9 cm)
license_or_reuse: Public domain (PD-art faithful reproduction)
relevance: The canon's first running-script model; also a lesson in what a copy is
annotation: Variable column spacing (front 13 lines looser, rear 15 tighter); stray-hair 賊毫/叉筆 strokes surviving the trace-and-fill copy method
designer_lesson: Copy fidelity is visible in texture: traced outlines vs free brushwork can be distinguished — and both are documented features, not flaws
limits: Wang Xizhi original lost; even the 神龍 seal is suspected a later addition (故宮 單國強); treat as tradition anchor, not autograph

title: 祭姪文稿 (Draft of a Requiem to My Nephew)
creator: Yan Zhenqing 顏真卿
license_or_reuse: Public domain (PD-art); NPM also distributes CC BY 4.0 album PDF (NPM-故書000060)
relevance: The canonical case for pressure/emotion correlation and draft authenticity
annotation: Visible corrections, insertions, ink-depletion within lines; pressure and agitation rise toward the later columns
designer_lesson: Documentary drafts gain authority from visible process; don't 'clean up' corrections when reproducing
limits: Emotion-readings are interpretive tradition (C), not measurement; Commons strip is 6903×400 — use NPM Open Data album for print resolution

title: 自敘帖 (Autobiographical Essay), wild cursive

license_or_reuse: CC BY 4.0 National Palace Museum Open Data (attribution required)

annotation: 65-page album PDF of IIIF images; thin-but-continuous centreline strokes; dry-brush splitting at radicals; re-dip rhythm visible across the roll
designer_lesson: 飛白 and ink rhythm cannot be faked by texture filters — reproduce facsimile or don't imitate
limits: Authenticity of the Taipei version is debated (three-versions controversy); 28.3×755 cm per NPM theme page

title: Inscriptions on the Stone Drums (石鼓文) — Ming/Qing rubbing pair

institution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York (original stones: Palace Museum, Beijing)

annotation: Even-weight concealed-tip seal line; erosion texture of stone clearly separable from brush line in the rubbing
designer_lesson: Teaches the difference between weathering and brushwork — vital when using rubbings as design texture
limits: Dating of the stones is unsettled (Duke Wen to Qin Shihuang era claims); rubbing ≠ the stone's current state

title: 祭姪文稿 (Draft of a Requiem for My Nephew)

limits: Surviving scroll is the autograph draft; condition darkened by age
